speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Ministry will consider requiring all drivers, both local and foreign, to attend periodic refresher courses; (b) whether the Ministry will consider enhancing preventive measures, such as but not limited to, the installation of speed limiters on all motor vehicles including passenger cars; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider imposing stricter non-financial criteria for ownership of vehicles and vehicle rentals.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs what measures are being taken to improve road safety education for both new and experienced drivers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs how is the Singapore Police Force ensuring the enforcement of traffic laws, particularly against reckless driving.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Government will consider imposing stiffer penalties on risky driving conduct; and (b) whether a major media campaign can be conducted to increase public awareness of responsible driving habits along with the new measures being put in place to curtail fatal road accidents.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs what support systems are in place for families of road accident victims, especially when the victim is a minor.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The recent Tampines accident which took two lives shocked and angered many Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I am sure I speak for all of us in saying we were all deeply saddened as well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Members have asked many questions, centred on: firstly, our road safety situation; secondly, adequacy of penalties to deter dangerous driving; thirdly, enforcement efforts; and fourthly, measures to improve road safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: First, Members asked for data on fatal accidents and their causes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There were 71 fatal accidents in the first half of 2023 and 60 in the second half of the year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The top causes of the fatal accidents between 2019 and 2023 were: firstly, failure to keep a proper lookout; and secondly, failure to have proper control of one's vehicle.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: An average of three fatal accidents per year, or about 2.4% of fatal accidents annually, were investigated under the offence of reckless or dangerous driving causing death.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: An average of 29 fatal accidents per year, or 27% of fatal accidents annually, were speeding-related.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Members may wish to refer to the Annual Road Traffic Situation Report on the Police's website, for more details on the situation in 2023.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Second, Members asked whether we intend to review and increase the penalties under the Road Traffic Act, or RTA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) had raised the penalties significantly in 2019.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: A repeat offender will be liable for up to 15 years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In addition, an offender could face a minimum 10 years of disqualification from driving, which begins only from the time that the offender is released from prison.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Thus a first offender in a serious case could be jailed for a maximum of eight years and not drive for 18 years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: What the laws provide today are already quite stiff.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We do regularly review different aspects of the framework.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In this context, we have been studying the adequacy of composition amounts and the demerit points framework.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Most people know about the regular enforcements that we have.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In addition, since last month, TP has progressively activated the speed enforcement function in red-light cameras across the island, especially at locations that are more accident-prone or violation-prone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: More than 800 speeding violations have been detected by these cameras thus far.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Whilst enforcement cameras are useful for deterrence, it is not feasible to install them at all traffic junctions and zebra crossings, given terrain limitations and other constraints.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked whether the reporting of traffic violations by the public can be made easier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The public may conveniently report traffic violations online via the Police's E-Services or Police@SG app, with supporting evidence such as video footage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: TP has been taking enforcement action based on such evidence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Fourth, Members asked about our plans to improve road safety and raised several suggestions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: To incentivise safe driving behaviour, eligible motorists may attend the Safe Driving Course and have four demerit points expunged from their record after completing the course.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The course aims to re-educate and correct the poor driving behaviours of motorists who have accumulated a significant number of demerit points.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim, can I request for you to take a seat first.

The following questions were moved earlier – Ms Joan Pereira asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Ministry will consider requiring all drivers, both local and foreign, to attend periodic refresher courses; (b) whether the Ministry will consider enhancing preventive measures, such as but not limited to, the installation of speed limiters on all motor vehicles including passenger cars; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider imposing stricter non-financial criteria for ownership of vehicles and vehicle rentals.

Mr Desmond Choo asked the Minister for Home Affairs in view of the recent spate of major road traffic fatal accidents (a) what are the typical causes of such accidents; (b) what mitigation plans will the Ministry implement; and (c) whether there is a need to raise the relevant penalties under the Road Traffic Act 1961.

Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) over the past five years, how many fatal accidents have occurred due to reckless driving and speeding; (b) whether there is a need to review the existing penalties under the Road Traffic Act 1961; (c) whether the Ministry and LTA will consider stricter enforcement measures or legislative changes to ensure greater accountability and discourage dangerous driving; and (d) whether there are plans to intensify campaigns or programmes in educating drivers on speeding and reckless driving and increase road safety awareness.
Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan asked the Minister for Home Affairs what measures are being taken to improve road safety education for both new and experienced drivers.
Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan asked the Minister for Home Affairs how is the Singapore Police Force ensuring the enforcement of traffic laws, particularly against reckless driving.

Mr Derrick Goh asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Government will consider imposing stiffer penalties on risky driving conduct; and (b) whether a major media campaign can be conducted to increase public awareness of responsible driving habits along with the new measures being put in place to curtail fatal road accidents.
Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan asked the Minister for Home Affairs what support systems are in place for families of road accident victims, especially when the victim is a minor.

Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo asked the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the significant increase of traffic accidents resulting in fatalities in 2023 and the recent road accident in Tampines that claimed lives, what measures can be taken to improve road safety for users.

Ms Tin Pei Ling asked the Minister for Home Affairs in view of the recent fatal traffic accidents (a) how will enforcement of road safety for both motorists and pedestrians be further enhanced; (b) whether the reporting of drivers' infringement of traffic rules by the public can be made easier; and (c) whether smart enforcement cameras can be installed at all major traffic junctions and zebra crossings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It works with various partners and stakeholders, including the Singapore Road Safety Council, SBS Transit and Grab, to organise events and campaigns to promote road safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We welcome more partners and stakeholders to join our road safety initiatives to develop a culture of responsible road usage.
Members asked how road infrastructure can be modified or improved to enhance safety.
TP works closely with the Land Transport Authority (LTA) on this.
The Ministry of Transport will provide details in its reply later.
Ms Pereira asked whether we will require all drivers to attend periodic refresher courses.
Only a minority of motorists are involved in accidents.
The very large majority of motorists stay offence-free for many years, if not, the entire period of their driving history.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry consider requiring the installation of speed limiters on vehicles or drivers new to Singapore roads?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For example, within two years of obtaining a driving licence, or maybe for foreigners, within two years of converting a driving licence to drive in Singapore?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I have shared in my answer, we feel that it is not necessary at this moment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, we will continue to monitor the situation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is with reference to the most tragic accident in Tampines.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Many of our colleagues in Tampines and Pasir Ris have received many comments from our residents, seeking answers on how we can prevent this similar incident from happening.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Without prejudicing the investigation, can the Minister of State share further with regard to this particular case, what are the steps taken to mitigate against such potential accidents and prevent such tragic cases from happening again?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: And secondly, can the Minister of State also share, compared to 10 to 15 years ago, especially in those particular areas, are our roads safer today?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If you look back and you look at the trend of the accidents, in fact, today, our roads are safer compared to 10 or 15 years ago.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The number of fatalities last year was lower, compared to 10 years ago, in 2013, for example, and the number of injury accidents last year was also lower than pre-pandemic years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With regard to the first question, I have also answered some parts of it in my main answer.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I also shared, we are looking further at the demerit points and the composition framework, to further enhance the road safety ecosystem.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The other part is, I think, as I have shared earlier, road safety is necessarily a shared responsibility.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I am very happy to see that over the years, more and more Community Partners have come on board to join in this effort.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Just yesterday morning, I was with Senior Minister of State Sim Ann to launch a very meaningful programme undertaken by her grassroots organisations, as well as with the stakeholders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: She and her grassroots' leaders noticed that the traffic situation in the Watten Estate and Hillcrest area would require some localised touch in regards to road safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, what they have done is, they have worked with the agencies to install reminders to motorists to say, "You will take one minute to arrive at the junction of Dunearn Road", for example.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, this gives that opportunity for the riders to internalise the time, so they do not have to rush, especially in areas where there are many other stakeholders who are vulnerable, like school children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For example, we have published a book for preschool students and we have been going around to preschools to engage the students, their parents and the teachers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also recently launched the "Reward the Sensible Motorists" campaign.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Yesterday, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and I rewarded a motorist, who was pleasantly surprised that he was stopped by TP to give commendation to him.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, these are things that I hope we can work together on, to really make the term "Road Safety is Necessarily a Shared Responsibility" alive for our people, so that we can help to save lives and bring goodness to people around us.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First of all, I would like to share my condolences to the families that were affected by the tragic events in Tampines.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first supplementary question is, in his reply, he mentioned that almost 27% of the cases were from speeding, or almost one-third of it.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And a related question to that is, I had asked in my original Parliamentary Question, whether there will be stricter enforcements or legislative changes and from that, to what extent or thresholds would the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and LTA look at to enhance the RTA going forward, in terms of threshold levels?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second supplementary question is in relation to road rage handling.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Minister of State mentioned that there will be enhanced road safety efforts, but can there be efforts to ensure that there is an embedding of how we handle road rage – as motorists, drivers or pedestrians.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, dealing with road rage and whether this can form a part of educating new and experienced drivers going forward?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will take the feedback in his second supplementary question.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We not only work with the stakeholders' agencies, we also work with the trade associations, like the Motor Traders Association of Singapore, and see how we can make things better and how to address it well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With regard to speeding related issues, in fact, if you look at the statistics, we publish some of them in TP's annual reports.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The post-pandemic average figure is higher than the pre-pandemic figure, mostly driven by high numbers in 2021, if you look at the figure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, from the average perspective, it is lower.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, it may go up and down, depending on the years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, 2023 is the lowest that we have.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The number of red-light running accidents as well – these are sometimes related to speeding – from 2020, we have 119; in 2021, 136; in 2022, we have 137; in 2023, we have 112.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, can I ask the Minister of State, how does TP treat these videos, whether these are considered sufficient evidence for TP to take enforcement actions on possible violations?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With the era of social media and also online platforms, TP embraces them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We look at some of this evidence and also, we are often being tagged whenever there are posts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We constantly try to look at how we can improve our platforms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Tin has shared some feedback and we have taken it back.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As for posting on social media, some of these platforms that we are familiar with, we look at it and we take that seriously, to investigate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But it does not mean we will just take on board everything that we see, what we want to see is part of the investigation process, so that we can enhance the evidential part of it, as well as we want to make sure that we navigate today's landscape together, with what we can find in technology.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: There are still quite a few hands up.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: I would ask Members to keep your questions brief and also your answers brief.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Because you can either proceed under RTA as careless driving, or you proceed under section 304A in the Penal Code.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: So, I see a disparity in some of these and so, how do we go about that, to decide the eventual punishment as meted out?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The second question, we also see, at some of these major junctions and areas that are a bit more vulnerable to accidents, this point of presence by TP, I was just wondering whether these days, is there a shortfall of TP officers or enforcement on the ground?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For the first question, of course, we have to look at all the evidence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the end of the day, the Courts' system is such that the Judges will have the different levers to look at.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, from our point of view, when we find there is an accident, we will look at the evidence and then we will relate the evidence to which part of the Act that we want to take on.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Similarly, for the case that we have, for the Tampines case.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, the number of TP officers has gone up.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Also, we deploy our officers based on the operational needs and they can only go out after they have received the necessary training.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is not easy to ride the bike.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: You need skills and you need to be able to develop this experience.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I must say, because I work very closely with TP, we have very good officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We know our weather is very hot and, sometimes, it rains heavily.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Sometimes, when I meet them after they come back from their operations, they are all sweating.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And, sometimes, when I visit, we see that there are TP officers conducting some speed camera operations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But when I get there and I speak to them, I find they have stood there for hours and sometimes under the hot sun.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, it is not easy work, but it is necessary so that we can keep our roads safe.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In addition to that, we also augment processes with technology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, today, we see a lot more use of cameras and also devices that will help them in their work.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: First, I think the Minister of State indicated there will be more use of cameras at traffic light junctions.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But how about stretches of roads where there are no traffic lights?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: In this House, I had asked about Woodlands Avenue 5 previously, where I have had residents post a lot of videos of what they believe to be speeding.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: We had asked for cameras because we know that TP are short on manpower.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But I think, at that time, they said the incidence rate was not above the average.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, in line with rolling out more cameras at junctions, will they also roll out more along roads?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The second supplementary question is whether or not the Minister of State would consider having more serious penalties for dangerous or careless driving where there is death or grievous bodily harm.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: For causing death, it is two to eight years, and one to five years for causing grievous hurt.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: This seems a little low for the seriousness of the injuries and so, whether we can consider increasing the penalties for that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I have shared in my answer, we feel that our penalties and punishment framework is already stiff.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If you compare it with other parts of the world, our road safety situation is actually much better than in many parts of the world.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And I have also shared that we regularly review the framework that we have.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The other thing about the area that the Member has shared with us, the process is that when we receive feedback, our TP officers will monitor the situation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We work with grassroots organisations and then we assess whether it is really that serious.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If we find that something that can be managed, we will make our presence there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And we will also try other levers to address the issue.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I thank the Member for sharing this with us.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I understand that the area, the road that the Member was sharing about, if there are no reminders, there are no enforcement efforts, those with no road safety behaviour may speed and may cause danger to the public.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The first question relates to the earlier question that my hon friend Mr Vikram has asked.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And I hear the Minister of State on the answer he gave that the Government intends to keep to the same punishments as per the current law.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: My second supplementary question is: would TP or MHA look into enhancing the current public education drive to promote safe driving, including more patience among drivers, to be more considerate to other road users?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I think all of us here would have frequently experienced that whenever the light changes to green, there will be immediately somebody pressing their honk.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: It is almost like they want to press the honk as soon as the light turns to green.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: That, to me, reflects on a very general symptom of impatience among drivers, perhaps not just at the traffic junction, but generally.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And I believe that this impatience is a frequent cause of accidents.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Also, in terms of being considerate to the users, for example, to encourage more heavy vehicles and goods vehicles not to keep right, but to try to keep left whenever possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And this is something that we want to ensure that we have – a fair and just system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, even in the hours of the day or night when there are no vehicles, accidents have happened.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, the whole idea is not about timing alone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we want to make sure we enhance the behaviour of people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have looked at the various factors of accidents, why accidents happened.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Essentially, it is about the lack of control of their vehicle.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: They did not look out sufficiently for traffic or their own presence along that road.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are many other factors that affect why accidents happen.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: One supplementary question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I wonder whether the Minister of State will agree with me that the public education efforts that the Government is undertaking could also focus a bit more on some aspects of the driving culture which I detect has a certain permissive attitude towards speed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: On any given day, if you are driving on the highway in lane one at the speed limit, cars will blow their horns at you and overtake you from the left.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Yes, indeed, it is something that we need to develop holistically as a society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we work together with the Singapore Kindness Movement, the Singapore Road Safety Council, as well as organisations around.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the end of the day, we need to internalise this whole element within each of us that there are people around us who are also using the road; it is not only us alone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And these people or road users have families and they are going to do their activities, the more care will be applied in the way we use our devices on the road.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, this is an ongoing journey that we want to continue.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I am very heartened, like what I shared, over the years, we are seeing more and more people coming on board to support this effort.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And if we look back, as I shared earlier, 10 or 15 years before till today, our roads are safer.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Speaker, I would like to ask the Minister of State whether they will consider a joint campaign or some joint trainings together with our recently set up mental well-being department.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: So, does the Minister of State see opportunities to collaborate with the Mental Well-being Taskforce on such matters?
